# circuitscaper

**circuitscaper** is circuit-theory landscape connectivity for R. You
work with `terra` rasters in R, while Julia handles the heavy lifting
under the hood. It offers two families of methods:

- **Circuitscape and Omniscape** (`cs_*()`, `os_*()`): the established
  tools, run through
  [Circuitscape.jl](https://github.com/Circuitscape/Circuitscape.jl) and
  [Omniscape.jl](https://github.com/Circuitscape/Omniscape.jl), with the
  same results as running them directly.
- **Dipole methods** (`dp_*()`, experimental): circuitscaper’s own
  methods for pairwise, omnidirectional and cross-era connectivity. They
  factor one circuit and solve many superposed source–sink pairs against
  it, so a map takes about 32 solves whatever the number of pairs, and
  each map comes with an estimate of its own noise. They compute a
  related but different quantity (squared rather than absolute current)
  and are not yet published; see the [Dipole
  methods](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/articles/dipole-methods.html)
  article.

Installation of Julia and its packages takes one line, and Julia threads
speed up Omniscape and the dipole methods on large landscapes.

> Note: **circuitscaper** is an independent R package and is not
> affiliated with the Circuitscape development team. Its `cs_*()` and
> `os_*()` functions wrap the excellent Julia tools developed by Brad
> McRae, Viral Shah, Tanmay Mohapatra, Ranjan Anantharaman, and
> collaborators.

## Installation

``` r

# 1. Install the R package from CRAN
install.packages("circuitscaper")
# or install the development version from GitHub
# remotes::install_github("matthewkling/circuitscaper")

# 2. Let the package install Julia and the necessary Julia libraries
library(circuitscaper)
cs_install_julia()

# (Or, for the dipole methods alone, just Julia)
# cs_install_julia(circuitscape = FALSE)
```

## Example

``` r

library(circuitscaper)
library(terra)

# Load an example resistance raster
resistance <- rast(system.file("extdata/resistance.tif", package = "circuitscaper"))

# Pairwise Circuitscape
# (result is a list containing the pairwise resistance matrix and current maps)
focal_sites <- matrix(c(10, 40, 40, 40, 25, 10), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
result <- cs_pairwise(resistance, focal_sites)
plot(result$current_map)
```

![](reference/figures/README-example-1.png)

``` r


# Omnidirectional connectivity across the whole landscape, with Omniscape's
# moving window and with random dipoles
# (each result is a multi-layer raster of current flow variables)
os <- os_run(resistance, radius = 10)
dp <- dp_omni(resistance, radius = 10, seed = 1)
plot(c(os$normalized_current, dp$normalized_current),
     main = c("os_run()", "dp_omni()"))
```

![](reference/figures/README-example-2.png)

## Functions

Choose by the question you’re asking; where both families answer it, the
[getting started
vignette](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/articles/getting-started.html)
helps choose between them.

| Question | Circuitscape and Omniscape | Dipole methods |
|----|----|----|
| How well connected are these sites, and through where? | [`cs_pairwise()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_pairwise.md) | [`dp_pairwise()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/dp_pairwise.md) |
| How does current spread from, or converge on, each site? | [`cs_one_to_all()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_one_to_all.md), [`cs_all_to_one()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_all_to_one.md) |  |
| How does movement flow between a source area and a destination? | [`cs_advanced()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_advanced.md) |  |
| Where are the corridors and barriers across the whole landscape? | [`os_run()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/os_run.md) | [`dp_omni()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/dp_omni.md) |
| How could habitat shift between climate eras, and along which routes? | [`os_run()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/os_run.md) with `os_condition(future = )` | [`dp_flux()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/dp_flux.md), [`dp_pathways()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/dp_pathways.md) |

Also:

| Function | Description |
|----|----|
| **[`os_condition()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/os_condition.md)** | Define conditions for conditional Omniscape connectivity |
| **[`dp_circuit()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/dp_circuit.md)** | Factor a circuit once, to reuse across dipole-method runs |
| **[`cs_setup()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_setup.md)** | Initialize the Julia session and set its threads (called automatically) |
| **[`cs_install_julia()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_install_julia.md)** | Install Julia and the required Julia packages |
| **[`cs_julia_available()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_julia_available.md)** | Check whether Julia, Circuitscape.jl, and Omniscape.jl are installed |

## Requirements

- R \>= 4.0
- Julia \>= 1.10 (installed automatically via
  [`cs_install_julia()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_install_julia.md))
- R packages: terra, JuliaConnectoR

- [Getting started
  vignette](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/articles/getting-started.html):

  circuit theory to model connectivity in ecology, evolution, and
  conservation. *Ecology*, 89(10), 2712-2724.

# Package index

## Circuitscape

Circuitscape’s four modes, run through Circuitscape.jl.

- [`cs_pairwise()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_pairwise.md)
  : Pairwise Circuitscape Analysis
- [`cs_one_to_all()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_one_to_all.md)
  : One-to-All Circuitscape Analysis
- [`cs_all_to_one()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_all_to_one.md)
  : All-to-One Circuitscape Analysis
- [`cs_advanced()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_advanced.md)
  : Advanced Circuitscape Analysis

## Omniscape

Moving-window connectivity, run through Omniscape.jl.

- [`os_run()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/os_run.md)
  : Run Omniscape Moving-Window Connectivity Analysis
- [`os_condition()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/os_condition.md)
  : Define a Condition for Conditional Omniscape Connectivity

## Dipole methods

circuitscaper’s own methods: pairwise, omnidirectional and cross-era
connectivity from superposed random dipoles on one factored circuit.
Experimental; see the Dipole methods article.

- [`dp_circuit()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/dp_circuit.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Prepare a Circuit for the Dipole Methods
- [`dp_omni()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/dp_omni.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Omnidirectional Connectivity From Random
  Dipoles
- [`dp_pairwise()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/dp_pairwise.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Pairwise Connectivity Among Focal Nodes From
  Random Dipoles
- [`dp_flux()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/dp_flux.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Cross-Era Net Flux
- [`dp_pathways()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/dp_pathways.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Cross-Era Gross Pathways From Random Dipoles

## Setup

Finding, installing and starting Julia.

- [`cs_setup()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_setup.md)
  : Set Up Julia
- [`cs_install_julia()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_install_julia.md)
  : Install Julia and Required Packages
- [`cs_julia_available()`](https://matthewkling.github.io/circuitscaper/reference/cs_julia_available.md)
  : Check if Julia and Required Packages Are Available
